turns.content: Four dihydrocinnoline precursors are oxidized to their aromatic products. Compound 2 is the 1,10-dimethyl analogue of compound 1 and has severe peri/bay methyl crowding, whereas compound 4 is the 3,8-dimethyl analogue and lacks that clash. How should oxidation-induced rigidity and planarity affect relative steric strain?
State the thermodynamic criterion for identifying the least-favorable oxidation, distinguishing product destabilization relative to its precursor from absolute product rigidity.
For compound 2, compare crowding in the reduced precursor and oxidized product and infer how the difference affects oxidation favorability.
Compare compounds 1, 3, and 4 against the same product-versus-precursor strain criterion. Does any have a comparable peri/bay penalty?
Complete the relative product-destabilization ranking and identify the least-favorable oxidation.
How strongly is that qualitative ranking supported without computed free energies, conformer populations, kinetics, solvent or temperature dependence, or an experimental ranking?
Check that the conclusion follows from relative product-versus-precursor destabilization rather than absolute rigidity alone.
Report the least-favorable oxidation, its spatial justification, and the remaining uncertainty.
